patterns_detected.description: An entity whose attribute set varies (by type or category, or as attribute rows), read by its key: DocumentDB stores each entity as one document of up to 16 MB with only the fields it has; it has no wildcard index, so each queried attribute needs its own index (Amazon DocumentDB Developer Guide, Quotas and limits; Functional differences).
Parent-child FK relationships with bounded child cardinality suitable for embedding as nested arrays. Eliminates JOINs entirely.
A grouped aggregate, or one over rows no key anchors, that maps to DocumentDB's aggregation pipeline ($group, $match, $project, $sort).
A query that reads JSON paths (JSON_EXTRACT, ->>, JSON_VALUE): the data is already semi-structured, and each path maps to a document field.

anti_patterns_detected.description: Queries joining 3 or more tables. Each join becomes a $lookup stage that reads the joined collection for the documents flowing through it, one stage per collection, with a nested-loop, hash or sort-merge algorithm (Amazon DocumentDB Developer Guide, Functional differences, $lookup); correlated $lookup needs DocumentDB 8.0.2 or later.
anti_patterns_detected.recommendation: Pre-denormalize via Extended Reference Pattern or write-time aggregation. Never chain $lookup operations.

anti_patterns_detected.description: Queries with NOT IN, <>, !=, NOT EXISTS, which map to $ne/$nin/$nor. Query planner version 2 and later use indexes for $ne, $nin and $not, so a negation is no worse on DocumentDB than on an engine where it is rarely index-selective (Amazon DocumentDB Developer Guide, Query planner).
anti_patterns_detected.recommendation: Redesign hot query paths to use positive equality operators ($eq, $in).

anti_patterns_detected.description: SQL window functions $setWindowFields serves (ROW_NUMBER, RANK, running totals): DocumentDB 8.0.2 or later on an instance-based cluster. LAG and LEAD ($shift) and NTILE (no bucketing window operator) run on no version, so they are a hard capability gap, not this entry (Amazon DocumentDB Developer Guide, Supported MongoDB APIs, operations, and data types).
anti_patterns_detected.recommendation: Use Computed Pattern (pre-calculated fields) or application-layer computation.

anti_patterns_detected.description: Queries with correlated subqueries. A correlated $lookup (let/pipeline) runs its sub-pipeline for each input document, and needs DocumentDB 8.0.2 or later on an instance-based cluster (Amazon DocumentDB Developer Guide, Supported MongoDB APIs, operations, and data types); otherwise pre-denormalize.
anti_patterns_detected.recommendation: Pre-denormalize at write time. Use Extended Reference Pattern to embed frequently co-accessed fields.

anti_patterns_detected.description: Self-referential FKs or recursive queries. $graphLookup runs on DocumentDB 8.0 instance-based clusters, not on 5.0 or earlier and not on elastic clusters (Amazon DocumentDB Developer Guide, Supported MongoDB APIs, operations, and data types).
anti_patterns_detected.recommendation: Use Materialized Path pattern (store ancestor path as string), or pre-flatten hierarchies at write time. Consider Neptune for true graph workloads.

pricing_assumptions: Standard storage I/O: $0.2 per million read/write requests

Read I/O: only cache misses billed, at the source's instance-wide buffer-cache hit ratio (99.989231%), not scaled to the target's memory (the source reported no memory size), billed at 99%. At least 1% of every read is billed as a miss.
No backups, snapshots, or data transfer included
